items.title: Topic Six Opens: Who Can Truly Guide Others to Freedom?

items.zh: 誰獎勝類生，及開出離道？於何住、何學，不懼後世死？
items.en: Who guides the superior kinds of beings, and opens the path of release? In what should one abide, and what should one train in, so as not to fear death in a future life?

items.zh: 戒慧、自薰修，具定、念、正直。斷諸愁、熾燃，正念、心解脫。能獎勝類生，及開出離道；住此、於此學，不懼後世死。
items.en: Precepts and wisdom, self-cultivated; possessed of concentration, mindfulness, and uprightness; having cut off sorrow's blaze; the mind liberated through right mindfulness — such a one truly guides the superior kinds of beings, and opens the path of release. Abiding in this, training in this, one no longer fears death in a future life.

items.title: The Four Classes, and Why Only the Buddha Is the True Guide

items.zh: 今此頌中，言勝類者，即是四種勝上姓類。一、婆羅門，二、剎帝利，三、吠舍，四、戍達羅。
items.en: In this verse, "the superior kinds" refers to the four superior classes: first, brahmins; second, kṣatriyas; third, vaiśyas; and fourth, śūdras.

items.zh: 以法、以正、以制、以導，教勝類生，故名為獎。此中顯示唯佛世尊能以法、以正、以制、以導，教勝類生。由此因緣，世尊自顯唯我獨為真獎導者。
items.en: Teaching the superior kinds of beings through the Dharma, through right refuge, through established precepts, and through guidance — this is called "guiding." This shows that only the Blessed One is able to teach the superior kinds of beings through the Dharma, through right refuge, through established precepts, and through guidance. For this reason, the Blessed One reveals that he alone is the true guide...

items.zh: 故為彼天作如是說，具戒、具慧以自薰修。
items.en: So he spoke thus to that god: complete in ethics and complete in wisdom, one perfumes and cultivates oneself.

items.zh: 又唯世尊能為四種勝上類生，宣說出離一切眾苦聖八支道。此中世尊亦自顯示是真說者。
items.en: And only the Blessed One is able to teach the four superior classes of beings the noble eightfold path that releases every kind of suffering. Here, the Blessed One likewise reveals himself as the true teacher.

items.title: Precepts, Wisdom, and Self-Cultivation: The First Three of Nine Qualities

items.zh: 云何具戒？謂佛世尊昔菩薩時，棄上妙欲，捨離居家，受持身語所有律儀。
items.en: What is "possessed of precepts"? It means that the Blessed Buddha, when formerly a bodhisattva, gave up the finest sensual pleasures, left household life behind, and upheld all bodily and verbal discipline.

items.zh: 云何具慧？謂即於彼受持身語律儀住者，起如是相，內正思惟，深心籌量，審諦觀察：今此世間多遭艱苦，所謂若生、若老，如經廣說。
items.en: What is "possessed of wisdom"? It means that one who, upholding this bodily and verbal discipline, abides [in the discipline of meditative absorption] raises such an image [as the object of meditation]: reflecting rightly within, weighing it deeply, examining it truly — recognising that this world constantly meets with hardship, whether through birth, through ageing, and so on, as the sutras explain at length.

items.zh: 云何自薰修？謂於往昔無量餘生，經三大劫阿僧企耶，於六波羅蜜多修習、善修習；由彼因緣，今無師自然心趣出離，又於眾緣所生諸行，以微妙智能隨悟入。
items.en: What is "self-cultivated"? It means that, across countless former lives spanning three incalculable eons, the six perfections were cultivated, and cultivated well. By this cause, in this life, without any teacher, the mind naturally inclined towards renunciation — and, towards all conditioned things arising from many causes, subtle wisdom was able to penetrate and awaken accordingly.

items.title: Concentration, Mindfulness, and Uprightness: Reaching the Stream

items.zh: 云何具定？謂能乃至離無所有處欲，證得非想非非想處。
items.en: What is "possessed of concentration"? It means being able to become free of desire even for the sphere of nothingness, and on to realising the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.

items.zh: 云何具念？謂依如是所得勝定，為斷見斷諸煩惱故，修四念住。即以如是所修念住為其導首，乃至修習三十七種菩提分法。
items.en: What is "possessed of mindfulness"? It means that, resting on this superior concentration attained, in order to sever the afflictions eliminated by the path of seeing, the four foundations of mindfulness are cultivated. Taking this cultivated mindfulness as the leading factor, the full thirty-seven factors of enlightenment are cultivated in turn.

items.zh: 云何正直？謂彼生起逆流正直聖八支道，能斷見斷所有煩惱，於逆流道得預隨流。
items.en: What is "uprightness"? It means that the noble eightfold path arises, upright and running counter to the current of saṃsāra, able to sever every affliction eliminated by the path of seeing — and, on this path running counter to the current, one becomes established in the stream of the noble ones.

items.title: Topic Six Concludes: From Sorrow's End to Full Awakening

items.zh: 云何永斷一切愁憂熾燃？謂從諦現觀俱得成不還者，又能永斷五下分結。瞋恚似順愁憂，貪欲似順熾燃，於如是等皆已永斷。
items.en: What is "permanently cutting off all sorrow's blaze"? It means that, from direct realisation of the truths, one becomes a non-returner, thereby permanently severing the five lower fetters. Aversion resembles and accords with sorrow; craving resembles and accords with blazing fire — both of these are now permanently severed.

items.zh: 云何正念？謂為永斷上分諸結，復更修習四種念住，乃至修習三十七種菩提分法。云何心解脫？謂已永斷上分結故，於二種障心善解脫，謂煩惱障、及所知障。其心如是善解脫故，得成如來應正等覺，
items.en: What is "right mindfulness"? It means that, in order to permanently sever the higher fetters as well, the four foundations of mindfulness are cultivated once more, and the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment cultivated in turn. What is "mind liberated"? It means that, the higher fetters now permanently severed, the mind becomes genuinely liberated from both obstructions — the afflictive obstruction and the cognitive obstruction. Because the mind is thus genuinely liberated, one attains the state of the Tathāgata, worthy of offerings, perfectly and fully awakened...

items.zh: 廣說如經。由此故能獎勝類生，開出離道。
items.en: As explained at length in the sūtra. Because of this, he can encourage those of superior kind and open the path of release.

items.zh: 諸有四種勝類，隨一於此聖教愛樂正行，為欲證得聖八支道，於三學中勤修學者，彼定能證聖八支道及涅槃果。由證彼故，不懼當來生老病死。復次，今當略辨上所說義。謂略顯示唯佛世尊，能令四類速得清淨。彼若於此能正修行，不唐捐故。又復示現如來聖教，善說正法及毘柰耶。又復示現佛是天人無上大師。
items.en: Whichever of the four superior classes delights in genuine practice within this teaching, and diligently trains in the three trainings in order to realise the noble eightfold path, will surely realise both the noble eightfold path and the fruit of nirvāṇa. Through this realisation, one no longer fears future birth, ageing, sickness, and death... This also reveals the Buddha as the unsurpassed teacher of gods and humans alike.

items.zh: 當知是名此中略義。
items.en: It should be understood that this is the summary meaning here.

items.title: Topic Seven Opens: What Actually Brings Renown, Wealth, Praise, and Friends

items.zh: 云何擅名譽？云何具珍財？云何獲美稱？云何攝親友？
items.en: How does one come to command renown? How does one come to possess treasured wealth? How does one come to earn genuine praise? How does one come to gather true friends?

items.zh: 持戒、擅名譽；布施、具珍財；諦實、獲美稱；惠捨、攝親友。
items.en: Keeping precepts, one commands renown; giving generously, one possesses treasured wealth; speaking truthfully, one earns genuine praise; giving freely, one gathers true friends.

items.zh: 云何持戒能擅名譽？
items.en: How does keeping the precepts win renown?

items.zh: 謂如有一，或男或女，具足尸羅及賢善法、乃至命終斷除殺罪、遠離殺生，如經廣說。乃至十方所有沙門、婆羅門等，常所稱歎。由是因緣，為諸國王、群臣、長者，乃至城邑聚落人民，恭敬供養。
items.en: It refers to one, man or woman, who fully possesses moral discipline and the qualities of a genuinely good person — abandoning the fault of killing, keeping far from taking life, until the very end of their days, as the sutras explain at length... down to being constantly praised by ascetics and brahmins in every direction. For this reason, they receive the reverent support of kings, ministers, elders, and the people of every town and village alike.

items.zh: 云何布施能具珍財？
items.en: How does giving bring wealth and treasure?

blocks.text: Fascicle 18 continues the essential-body verses: a deva asks, and the Buddha (or the treatise) answers in verse, followed by explanation. Today: who can truly guide beings to freedom, and, briefly, how one gains renown. In this fascicle Ru-Yi translates the verses and the shorter explanations; several long explanations are missing from Ru-Yi's translation; we supply our own translation and also summarise them.

The deva asks: who guides the superior kinds of beings, and in what should one train so as not to fear death in a future life? The answer lists nine qualities: precepts, wisdom, self-cultivation, concentration, mindfulness, uprightness, the end of sorrow's blaze, right mindfulness, and a liberated mind.

"The superior kinds" are the four classes of human society: brahmins, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras. Master Cháng Bǎi: they are "superior births" compared with the three lower realms. To "guide" is to teach through the Dharma, refuge, precepts (制), and concentration and wisdom (導). Only the Buddha teaches all four classes the eightfold path; his great disciples, like Śāriputra, transmit it.

The Buddha as bodhisattva gave up the finest pleasures and kept bodily and verbal discipline (**precepts**); contemplated deeply (**wisdom**: Venerable Miào Jìng: the two truths); had cultivated the six perfections over three incalculable aeons, so that in this life his mind turned to renunciation "without any teacher" (**self-cultivated**). Master Cháng Bǎi: when conditions ripen, it is "like a ripe melon dropping from its stem".

**Concentration** reaches up to the peak of existence; **mindfulness** is the four foundations, cultivated to cut the 112 afflictions abandoned by seeing; **uprightness** is the eightfold path running "against the current of saṃsāra".

"Aversion resembles sorrow; craving resembles blazing fire." The non-returner has cut both. Then right mindfulness cuts the higher fetters, and the mind is liberated. Master Cháng Bǎi: for a bodhisattva, liberation from both the afflictive and the cognitive obstructions makes one a Tathāgata. Such a one "does not fear death": Master Cháng Bǎi: with no further existence, there is no future birth, ageing, sickness, and death to fear.

A new question: how does one gain renown, wealth, praise, and friends? "Keeping precepts, one commands renown." Master Cháng Bǎi tells how children who saw Mahākāśyapa, so pure in conduct, would offer him their treats.

quiz.q: In "possessed of concentration, mindfulness, and uprightness," what attainment does Master Cháng Bǎi equate with "uprightness"?
options: the arising of the eightfold path against the current of saṃsāra, severing what is cut by seeing — stream-entry
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: thereby the eightfold noble path arises against the current of birth and death, severing all afflictions eliminated by seeing — one attains stream-entry.

quiz.q: In "having cut off sorrow's blaze," which afflictions does Master Cháng Bǎi assign to "sorrow" and to "blaze"?
options: sorrow is craving, blaze is aversion
bitter aversion causes inner sorrow; fiery craving causes inner blazing
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: no longer is inner sorrow stirred by bitter aversion, nor inner blazing by fiery craving. The prose in §5 likewise says aversion resembles sorrow and craving resembles blazing fire.

quiz.q: "Abiding in this, training in this, one no longer fears death in a future life" — how do the two masters explain "no fear"?
options: Cháng Bǎi: realising nirvāṇa, no further rebirth, no fear of future birth and death; Miào Jìng: though amid birth, ageing, sickness, and death, the mind has none of them, so there is no fear
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: because nirvāṇa is realised, there is no further existence, so one does not fear the suffering of future birth, ageing, sickness, and death. Venerable Miào Jìng: though you are amid birth, ageing, sickness, and death, your mind has none of them — so there is no fear.

quiz.q: In "through the Dharma, through right refuge, through established precepts, and through guidance," how do the masters gloss 制 and 導?
options: 制 is precepts; 導 is concentration and wisdom, teaching by them
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: 制 is precepts; 導 is concentration and wisdom — teaching learners by concentration and wisdom is "through guidance." Venerable Miào Jìng says the same. The English renders 以正 "through right refuge" and 以制 "through established precepts."

quiz.q: What does the treatise say "self-cultivated" means?
options: across three incalculable eons the six perfections were cultivated well, so in this life without a teacher the mind turned naturally to renunciation and subtle wisdom penetrated conditioned things
quiz.why: "Across countless former lives spanning three incalculable eons, the six perfections were cultivated, and cultivated well. By this cause, in this life, without any teacher, the mind naturally inclined towards renunciation." Venerable Miào Jìng: "cultivated" is the outer ordinary stage, "cultivated well" the inner; or ordinary versus noble stages.

quiz.q: How many conceptually arisen afflictions does Master Cháng Bǎi say are severed on the path of seeing?
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: added together there are 112 conceptually arisen afflictions — these are the afflictions severed on the path of seeing.

quiz.q: What does Master Cháng Bǎi illustrate with the story of Mahākāśyapa?
options: he was foremost in psychic power
his precepts were so pure that everyone who saw him rejoiced — precepts bring renown
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: Mahākāśyapa kept the precepts purely, and everyone who saw him, monastics included, felt joy. Children who saw him would offer him their treats.
